main_text.p: ci vocant: &,quæ utriusque particeps quodammodo uidetur esse, Medicinam, quippe quæ tum in naturæ obseruatione, tum in agédo, ut miscendo, secando, & urendo fere posita est. Ac philosophia quidem duplex est: naturalis, quæ in naturæ obseruatione: & moralis, quę in uita (ut ait Cicero) & moribus uersatur. Naturalem porrò, quoniam ea neq; ad Reipublicæ gubernationem, neque (ut Socrates docuit) ad bene uiuendum quicquam conducebat, & in recondi-tis ac tenebricosis quibusdā disputationibus, quę magna ex

page.notes: The head line reads "IVRISCONSVLTVS." and was normalised to IURISCONSULTUS. The word at the line end "ut mi" / "fcendo" is printed without a hyphen; read as "miscendo" (long s as plain s). "agédo" is printed with an acute accent over the e. The first line starts mid-sentence, so the paragraph continues from the previous page. The sentence is cut off at the foot ("quę magna ex") and continues on the next page. No catchword or signature is visible.
